gen_risks.description: Flood‑induced surge in non‑performing loans erodes capital adequacy of microfinance banks, threatening liquidity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Activate CRF contingent liquidity immediately; maintain capital buffers; use parametric insurance; monitor NPL trends closely.
gen_risks.evidence: NPLs of MFBs surged by 25.7% after the 2022 floods, eroding capital adequacy (section 9).

gen_risks.description: CRF may lack sufficient capital if multiple extreme flood events occur during the project period.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct annual stress tests; secure additional donor or private capital; retain insurance backstop; set aside reserve funds.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF capitalized to meet contingent financing needs; expansion requires additional capital (sections 21‑30).

gen_risks.description: Delay in activating CRF triggers due to slow data provision from third‑party providers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pre‑establish data‑sharing agreements with providers; define strict timelines; use real‑time monitoring; have backup data sources.
gen_risks.evidence: Data required to evaluate triggers will be provided by third‑party service providers (section 31).

gen_risks.description: Governance risk: SBP as trustee may face conflicts of interest or capacity constraints.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define clear fiduciary duties; create independent oversight committee; enforce regular external audits; adopt conflict‑of‑interest policies.
gen_risks.evidence: SBP will be the executing agency and trustee, selected after extensive due diligence (section 38).

gen_risks.description: Legal risk: Amendments to the Trust Deed require Association consent, potentially delaying actions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Obtain pre‑approval for likely amendments; maintain open communication with the Association; include emergency amendment clause.
gen_risks.evidence: Trust Deed cannot be amended without prior written consent of the Association (Legal Covenants).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient qualified agritech firms may limit the Innovative Agricultural Liquidity product’s effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Run transparent competitive AFIC selection; keep a backup list of ATCs; provide capacity‑building support to selected firms.
gen_risks.evidence: AFIC will identify five to six ATCs to partner with MFPs (section 26).

gen_risks.description: MFPs may not meet eligibility criteria for CRF liquidity, reducing uptake.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer flexible eligibility thresholds; assist MFPs in documenting flood exposure; monitor uptake and adjust criteria as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Only MFPs with active portfolios in qualifying flood‑impacted areas will be eligible (section 28).

gen_risks.description: Gender target (≥55% women beneficiaries) may not be achieved, limiting social impact.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set gender quotas; track disbursements gender‑disaggregated; enforce higher borrowing cost penalty for non‑compliance; conduct gender‑focused outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: Ensure at least 55% of beneficiaries are women; higher borrowing cost if deviation (section 49).

gen_risks.description: Annual decision not to purchase parametric insurance backstop could reduce CRF’s capacity during extreme events.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate a dedicated budget line; perform yearly financial review; negotiate multi‑year insurance contracts to lock coverage.
gen_risks.evidence: Decision to secure parametric insurance for the CRF will be undertaken annually by the Oversight Committee (section 30).

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability may impair MFPs’ ability to repay and maintain capital adequacy.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor macro indicators; adjust liquidity provisions accordingly; coordinate with Ministry of Finance for fiscal support; diversify funding sources.
gen_risks.evidence: Impact of shocks exacerbated by macroeconomic crisis since 2019; sector growth receded to 2.4% in 2023 (sections 8‑9).

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing pooled and child accounts could postpone CRF capitalization.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare account‑setup plan before project start; assign dedicated treasury team; obtain bank approvals early.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient will establish a pooled account with segregated child accounts; funds front‑loaded for CRF capitalization (section 43).

gen_risks.description: Inaccurate flood modelling data may trigger inappropriate CRF disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use multiple modelling sources; validate models annually; incorporate ground‑truth data; set conservative trigger thresholds.
gen_risks.evidence: Risk modelling will be the basis for CRF operations and trigger thresholds (section 37).

gen_risks.description: Increased agricultural lending could lead to higher fertilizer and pesticide use, causing localized environmental degradation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include environmental safeguards in loan terms; promote climate‑smart agronomy; monitor soil and water quality; enforce negative list.
gen_risks.evidence: Cumulative impacts may increase use of fertilizers, pesticides, affecting air and water quality (section 54).

gen_risks.description: Grievance Redress Service may be ineffective, leading to stakeholder dissatisfaction and reputational risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear GRS procedures; train staff; publicize channels; monitor complaint resolution times and satisfaction.
gen_risks.evidence: Establishment of a functional grievance redress mechanism to be integrated fully (section 50).

gen_risks.description: Currency fluctuations between PKR and USD could erode the real value of the CRF capital.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hedge currency exposure; maintain a reserve buffer; conduct periodic re‑valuation of capital in PKR terms.
gen_risks.evidence: Exchange Rate Effective Jan 31 2025: PKR 278.64 = US$1 (datasheet).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private sector participation may limit additional funding needed for CRF sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop attractive terms for private investors; showcase pilot successes; engage private sector early through outreach events.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF will crowd in additional funds from government, donors, etc., to mitigate climate risks (section 39).

gen_risks.description: Expanding CRF coverage to drought or heat may be constrained by lack of data and financing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create phased risk‑modelling roadmap; secure contingent financing in advance; pilot additional risk products before full rollout.
gen_risks.evidence: Enhancing scope to other climate risks requires additional capital and adequate risk modelling (sections 30‑31).

gen_risks.description: Political changes could reduce GoP commitment to the CRF and related policy alignment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Obtain multi‑year legislative endorsement; embed CRF in national policy frameworks; maintain broad stakeholder coalition.
gen_risks.evidence: Project aligns with GoP development priorities; implementation subject to GoP approval (section 3).

gen_risks.description: Compliance with ESS 9 (Financial Intermediaries) may cause procedural delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early compliance review; align project design with ESS 9 requirements; obtain necessary approvals promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: ESS 9: Financial Intermediaries Relevant (datasheet).

gen_risks.description: Gaps in monitoring and evaluation data could hinder tracking of PDO indicators.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen MIS; set data‑quality standards; train staff on data collection; conduct independent verification audits.
gen_risks.evidence: M&E will use bi‑annual reviews, financial audit, MIS, beneficiary surveys (section 41).

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is Substantial. The political context in Pakistan remains fluid. However, there has been significant decline in political uncertainty and associated policy instability in recent months, especially in the backdrop of the general elections. Given that a new government took the helm recently and the fact that policy priorities are still being defined, political risks, in particular in the context of the project, remain substantial.
gt_risks.mitigation: In the implementation stage, the risks will be mitigated through frequent monitoring and oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is High. While fiscal consolidation measures have supported short-term stabilization, macroeconomic risks remain high amid a high debt burden (72 percent of GDP), heavy financial sector exposure to government debt, large external financing needs, weak confidence, and little progress with structural reforms. Significant risks include potential worsening of external conditions, further natural disasters, and a slowdown or reversals in policy adjustment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Risks are partly mitigated by government commitment to implementation of reforms under the ongoing International Monetary Fund program, World Bank support to structural policy reforms in the fiscal and power sectors, strong government commitment to the reforms supported by the operation, and the availability of dedicated World Bank technical assistance to implement key reforms.
